title: Adaptive page-aligning KV cache and GPU prefetch controller
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Implement a paged/blocked KV cache design that aligns cache page boundaries to GPU DMA-friendly block sizes and couples an adaptive GPU prefetch controller to reduce hot-path stalls and OOMs during continuous batching. This ticket covers data structures, placement strategy, prefetch heuristics, and integration with the existing slab-backed allocator used for batch KV slices.

Background:
- Recent production incidents show intermittent spike in tail latency when large batched queries trigger on-demand GPU transfers and kernel serialization.
- Current slab allocator/kv implementation exhibits fragmentation and suboptimal transfer granularity that increases host->device memcpy overhead.

Design proposal summary:
1) Paged KV layout: split long KV sequences into fixed-size pages (configurable; default 64KB host contiguous pages). Pages are aligned to 4K/64K depending on NIC/GPU DMA alignment for reduced transfer overhead. Each page contains a set of KV blocks (block is a contiguous range of KV cache entries for a particular request). Pages are the unit of eviction and prefetch.

2) Block-level indexing: Maintain a lightweight page table (per-GPU shard) mapping page_id -> metadata (owner request ids, last-access-ts, hot-score). The table is stored in host RAM and persisted in lightweight form in GPU pinned memory for fast lookups during hot-path checks.

3) Adaptive prefetch controller: a background controller observes continuous batching patterns and issues proactive page transfers to GPU when predicted batch demand exceeds a low-water mark. Heuristics combine: recent reuse frequency, request arrival rate, and batch composition probability. Controller supports two modes: conservative (favor memory headroom) and eager (favor API latency). Mode is chosen by route-level SLO policy.

4) Eviction and fallback strategy: Eviction happens at page granularity. We implement a hybrid eviction: LRU among cold pages with size-aware compaction for partially-filled pages. When GPU memory is constrained, controller can downgrade pages to compressed-host storage (quantized cache) or move them to device-local spill (dedicated NVMe cache) if configured for Dedicated/Private deployments.

5) GPU paging integration: Use pinned host buffers and batched cudaMemcpyAsync streams (or equivalent backend) with page-aligned sizes to maximize PCIe/NVLink throughput. When available, use driver-level prefetch/advice (e.g., cudaMemPrefetchAsync or mmap-like hinting) to reduce page faulting. For VMs using iommu or host pinned UVM, fall back to aligned staged copies to avoid expensive per-page faulting.

6) Continuous batching interaction: During batch assembly, the router consults the page table to decide whether all required pages are resident. If missing pages exceed the per-batch miss threshold, the batch assembly will either: a) split the batch (small immediate batch + background prefetch) or b) trigger a prioritized prefetch path to avoid blocking the critical batch kernel. The prefetch controller aims to keep miss-induced blocking < 1% of batches under P50 SLO.

Implementation milestones:
- M1: Data model and page table proto; API and invariants (2d)
- M2: Pinned-buffer transfer primitives + aligned transfer test harness (3d)
- M3: Eviction + compaction + storage-tier fallback (5d)
- M4: Adaptive prefetch controller + SLO policy hooks (4d)
- M5: Integration tests, perf benchmarks, and rollout plan (3d)

Observability and instrumentation:
- Add per-page metrics: last_access_ts, hot_score, resident(bool), bytes_transferred, transfer_latency_ms.
- Dashboard: page residency heatmap, prefetch hit/miss rate, batch-blocking incidents (Datadog link below).

Benchmarks and targets (internal perf runs):
- Target: reduce batch-assembly median stall caused by KV transfers from ~14ms to <=3ms for 512-token average sequences.
- Target: reduce OOM-induced request failures by 70% under mixed traffic (40% long-context, 60% short).
- Target: maintain throughput within -5% of baseline while lowering per-token transfer cost by >=25% via alignment and batching.

Rollout plan:
- Canary on internal staging with a single regional host pool (canary tag runtime-1.22-canary-1).
- Observe mem pressure and prefetch error rates for 72h.
- Gradual ramp: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over two weeks with quick rollback flag.

- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Paged+KV+Design
- Perf dashboard (canary): https://datadog.redwood.ai/dash/runtime/paged-kv-canary
- Initial prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1128
acceptance_criteria: Page table implemented and exposed behind a feature flag
Aligned pinned-buffer transfer primitives pass microbenchmarks that show >=15% throughput improvement vs baseline unaligned copies
Adaptive prefetch controller reduces batch-assembly blocking in staging to <1% of batches for target load profile
Eviction path supports compressed-host fallback and does not regress 99th-percentile latency by more than 5%
End-to-end canary run for 72h with monitored memory safety (no new OOM regression) and validated rollback path
